name: Airbnb New User Bookings (Kaggle competition data itself, not a repo)
what_it_holds: train_users_2.csv / test_users.csv (~275k Airbnb user signups 2010-2014 with device, marketing channel, demographics, and first-booking destination country), sessions.csv (~10M web/app action-type events for a subset of users, 2014), age_gender_bkts.csv, countries.csv. Checked ~10 GitHub mirrors of solutions (Samer-Haddad/COMP9417-Project, pc90/Airbnb-New-User-Bookings---Kaggle-Competition, karthikhegde05/Airbnb-new-user-booking-competition, MadhumitaRoy/AirbnbNewUserBookings_Kaggle_Multi-Classification, ahmedsaeedsaid/Airbnb-New-User-Bookings-kaggle, rtlatimer/Airbnb-New-User-Bookings-Kaggle, Maram-Elsayed/Airbnb-New-User-Bookings-Kaggle, markrofail/airbnb-new-user-bookings-kaggle-, chriszeng8/Airbnb-New-User-Bookings-Kaggle-2016, RyanKopa/Airbnb-New-User-Bookings-Kaggle-Competition) via gh api contents listings on 4 of them plus repo browsing on the rest: NONE commit the raw CSVs, all contain only notebooks/scripts/submission images that assume the Kaggle data is downloaded separately (which requires a Kaggle login, out of scope per the sanctioned-sources rule).
why_useful: If the raw files existed in a repo they would be a pre-account-freeze (2010-2014) global user-acquisition and session-behavior panel for Airbnb itself -- interesting for host/guest engagement history (gap 15/company-structure adjacent, gap 5 engagement) -- but the data is 10+ years stale (pre-2015, well before the forecast window) and every mirror checked is a solutions notebook with no committed data, so this fails the cataloguing bar as a GitHub asset. Flagging only so nobody re-searches this exact query expecting a hit.
geography: Global (destination countries), user base skews US signups
size_hint: ~275k users, ~10M session rows (on Kaggle, not on GitHub)
license: Kaggle competition rules (non-commercial); no data license attached in any mirror
themes: Kaggle competitions and datasets on travel demand forecasting mirrored on GitHub (Expedia, Trivago, Booking, Airbnb new-user bookings, hotel demand)
why_all: If the raw files existed in a repo they would be a pre-account-freeze (2010-2014) global user-acquisition and session-behavior panel for Airbnb itself -- interesting for host/guest engagement history (gap 15/company-structure adjacent, gap 5 engagement) -- but the data is 10+ years stale (pre-2015, well before the forecast window) and every mirror checked is a solutions notebook with no committed data, so this fails the cataloguing bar as a GitHub asset.
